Bee die-offs started making the news back in the early 2000s (after the press decided that africanized honeybees were no longer some kind of existential threat). No one knew what caused them and scientists started attempting to determine what was going on.

Lots of different things were postulated and claims were made that it was mites, that it was genetics, that it was a fungus, that it was pesticides, that it was cell phone radiation, that it was some combination of the afore.

The long and short is that bees are absolutely critical to agriculture and that understanding what things could endanger them is kind of important. Everything else is pretty much speculation at this point.

The 1970 FIFA World Cup was the ninth FIFA World Cup, the quadrennial international football championship for men's national teams. Held from 31 May to 21 June in Mexico, it was the first World Cup tournament staged in North America, and the first held outside Europe and South America.

The tournament was won by Brazil, which defeated another two-time former champion, Italy, 4–1 in the final in Mexico City. The win gave Brazil its third World Cup title, which allowed them to permanently keep the Jules Rimet Trophy, and a new trophy was introduced in 1974. The victorious team, led by Carlos Alberto and featuring players such as Pelé, Gérson, Jairzinho, Rivellino, and Tostão, is often cited as the greatest-ever World Cup team. They achieved a perfect record of wins in all six games in the finals, as well as winning all their qualifying fixtures.
